n: Solomon seals a political alliance with Egypt by marrying Pharaoh’s daughter — a sign of Israel’s new international importance. But marrying foreign wives would later turn his heart; the Joseph Smith Translation adds that the Lord was not pleased with this marriage.

f.g: Formed an alliance by marriage. JST: “And the Lord was not pleased with Solomon, for he made affinity with Pharaoh.”

n: Because there was no temple yet, the people worshipped at “high places” — hilltop shrines. These were tolerated for a time but later became centers of idolatry.

f.g: Hilltop or elevated sites of worship, often with an altar.

f.w: there was no house built unto the name of the LORD

n: Solomon loved the Lord and followed David’s example — with one reservation: he also worshipped at the high places. The word “only” hints at a crack that will later widen.

f.g: A quiet qualification — his devotion was real but not yet complete.

n: Solomon goes to Gibeon, the most important high place because the tabernacle of Moses was there, and offers a thousand burnt offerings.

f.g: A lavish act of worship, perhaps over several days.

n: That night the Lord appears to Solomon in a dream with an open invitation: “Ask what I shall give thee.” What we ask for reveals what we truly value.

f.w: the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream
Ask what I shall give thee

n: Solomon begins with gratitude, praising God’s loyal love to David, who walked faithfully, and for placing David’s son on the throne.

f.g: Hebrew ḥesed — steadfast, covenant love.

n: He humbly admits he feels like a little child, unsure how to lead. Recognizing one’s own inadequacy is the beginning of real wisdom.

f.w: I am but a little child
how to go out or come in
f.g: How to lead, especially in daily affairs and in war.

n: He feels the weight of leading God’s chosen people, too numerous to count.
His request: an “understanding heart” — literally a “hearing heart” — so he can judge rightly and tell good from evil. It is a model prayer for anyone with responsibility.

f.g: Hebrew lev shomea — a listening, obedient heart.

f.w: that I may discern between good and bad

n: The Lord is pleased with Solomon’s request.
God notes what Solomon did not ask for — long life, wealth, or victory over enemies — but wisdom to govern justly.

f.g: To understand what is just and to make fair decisions.

n: God grants him a wise and discerning heart beyond anyone before or after him.

f.w: a wise and an understanding heart

n: God also gives what he did not ask for — riches and honor greater than any other king. Seeking first what matters most brings other blessings too.

f.w: that which thou hast not asked

n: But one blessing is conditional: if Solomon walks in God’s ways as David did, God will lengthen his life.

f.w: if thou wilt walk in my ways

n: Solomon wakes and realizes it was a revelatory dream. He goes to Jerusalem, worships before the ark, and holds a feast for his servants.

f.g: Offerings shared in a fellowship meal with God and others.

n: Now comes a test of the gift. Two prostitutes — women of the lowest status — come to the king for judgment. Even they could appeal directly to the king.

f.g: Prostitutes.

n: The first woman explains that both women live in the same house and she gave birth there.

f.w: I was delivered of a child
f.g: I gave birth.

n: Three days later the other woman also gave birth. No one else was in the house — so there are no witnesses.

f.g: No one else; no outsider who could testify.

n: The other woman’s baby died in the night because she rolled over on it while sleeping.

f.g: She lay on it and smothered it.

n: The first woman claims the other secretly swapped the babies while she slept.

f.g: Arms or lap — close beside her.

n: In the morning she found a dead baby beside her, but looking closely, she knew it was not hers.

f.g: To nurse my baby.

n: The second woman denies everything, and they argue back and forth before the king. It is one word against another.
Solomon summarizes the stalemate: each claims the living child.

f.g: Solomon carefully restates both claims, showing he has listened.

n: Then he calls for a sword.

f.g: A shocking order meant to reveal the women’s hearts.

n: He orders the living baby cut in two and divided between them — a test designed to reveal true love.

f.w: Divide the living child in two

n: The real mother, moved with love, begs the king to give the baby to the other woman rather than kill him. The other woman says to divide him. True love would rather lose than see the child harmed.

f.w: her bowels yearned upon her son
f.g: Her deepest compassion was stirred; the Hebrew word is related to “womb.”
In no way; by no means.

n: Solomon declares that the woman who wanted the child to live is the mother. Wisdom saw through to the heart.
All Israel hears of the judgment and stands in awe, recognizing that God’s wisdom was in their king. The dream at Gibeon has been confirmed in action.

f.w: the wisdom of God was in him

f.g: Here, held in reverent respect.
